title: UPDATE: Dev's Google AI Hack Transcribes 1 Hour of Audio in 13 Seconds

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
A developer repurposed the EmbeddingGemma 2 multimodal model into a speech-to-text tool that delivers 288x real time speed on a base M3 MacBook Air. By exploiting the way the model maps audio and spoken words into a shared vector space, the tool can transcribe one hour of recording in approximately 13 seconds without using a cloud server.

The 740M parameter model, released by Google under an Apache 2.0 license, supports a new wave of local Mac applications including the search tool DigUp and Google's own Foresight app. Recent community implementations show the model sorting roughly 620 posts per second on the Apple M5 Pro Neural Engine. The architecture unifies text, image, audio, and video, allowing it to outperform some specialist models twice its size on various benchmarks.

selectedTweets.bestBit: transcribes an hour of audio in about 13 seconds: 288× real time
selectedTweets.text:
I turned @googlegemma  EmbeddingGemma 2, an embedding model, into a speech-to-text model, and it turned out to be one of the fastest STT models you can run on device. 

On a base M3 MacBook Air it transcribes an hour of audio in about 13 seconds: 288× real time.

The idea came in March with Gemini Embedding 2. It puts text, images, audio and video into one shared space, so a spoken word lands right next to the written word. If that's true, you should be able to read a transcript straight out of the embedding model. I couldnt tried it then, but last week EmbeddingGemma 2 came out as an open model, so I tried it.

selectedTweets.bestBit: outperforming some specialist models more than twice its size
selectedTweets.text:
At 740M parameters, it’s competitive across benchmarks – even outperforming some specialist models more than twice its size.

Developers can use it to add multimodal search to their apps – like finding moments in a video using a voice memo – or pair it with Gemma 4 for private, on-device RAG.

EmbeddingGemma 2 is released under an Apache 2.0 license. Check out the weights on @HuggingFace and @Kaggle.

Find out more → https://t.co/lRsjbvR5VB
